headline: The challenger always fights as themselves
lede: VIPER PIT's online char-select got arcade law: a challenger's pick can no longer be dropped, overwritten, or lost to a reconnect — and the live two-Chrome drive that proved it found two more bugs the code-reading note never saw.

notes.text: A FIGHT press before the challenger picks now DEFERS the launch (select shows AWAITING CHALLENGER'S PICK…); the pick, whenever it lands, starts both boxes on the guest's REAL fighter — the IronRing #1761 gate law, ported to ViperPit, with a Node state machine + a named mutant keeping it honest.

The relay itself had never forwarded 'pick': the FORWARD_TYPES allowlist in relay/core.js silently dropped every challenger pick in production, in any order. Allowlisted and pinned both ways; this also un-blocks IRON RING's #1761 wire, which ships the same packet type.

Two more live-drive catches: the unmount teardown called net.lobby.destroy — a function that never existed — so a leaked socket could hold seat 1 forever (now the proven room.reset() pattern); and a reconnecting challenger re-declares its pick on re-seat, so choices survive their own retries. IRON RING's identical latent leak filed as #2478.

New live tier: npm run vipernet drives two headless Chromes over the local relay — race, pre-pick and ghost scenarios, socket-level logging, zero page errors: 13/13. viperpitcheck grows to 441, mutants 290/290 green on main.
